page: Microsoft Azure D4ls_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Dlsv7 family. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz, it features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it supports Premium Storage for remote disk attachments.

Benchmark data indicates a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-threaded operations perform strongly, as evidenced by gzip compression at 34.6 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.78 GB/sec. However, multi-core scaling is limited, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression both falling into the weak category. Memory bandwidth is also mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth is weak at 335.78 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth reaches an average tier of 45.33 GB/sec. Passmark CPU, encryption, and database benchmarks consistently register in the average range.

The D4ls_v7 offers a low-memory compute profile, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles and high single-core clock speeds without demanding large memory footprints. It is suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded data processing, and basic database operations, as demonstrated by its average static web serving throughput of 8.6 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 8.2 million operations per second. However, it is poorly suited for memory-intensive applications or complex machine learning tasks, with 7B LLM text generation speeds falling to a poor 5.03 tokens per second.
